holidays.name: National Wiggle Your Toes Day
holidays.description: Kick off your shoes and socks and give your piggies some attention. Today is a day to flex, stretch, and wiggle your toes just because you can. Toes are small, but they do a lot of work.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a favorite on quirky holiday calendars, and it is a good excuse to go barefoot.
holidays.funFact: Each human foot has 26 bones. That means your two feet hold about a quarter of all the bones in your body.

holidays.name: National Root Beer Float Day
holidays.description: Today is for the fizzy, creamy treat made by dropping a scoop of vanilla ice cream into a frosty glass of root beer. Grab a straw and a long spoon and dig in.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance. It is often linked to the invention of the 'Black Cow' float in 1893, when Frank Wisner supposedly saw snow-capped Cripple Creek Mountain and added ice cream to soda.
holidays.funFact: In some parts of the world, a root beer float is called a 'Black Cow.' Some places also make a version with cola, called a 'Boston Cooler' or 'Brown Cow.'

holidays.name: National Fresh Breath Day
holidays.description: A day for minty confidence. It encourages you to brush, floss, and freshen up before you chat with anyone. Keep a pack of mints handy.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It fits well with the oral-hygiene awareness days that appear on many calendars.
holidays.funFact: Ancient Egyptians made early breath mints by mixing herbs and spices such as frankincense and myrrh with honey.
